newsitem.title: USA: Zebra, Eltron fall, merger off.
newsitem.headline: Zebra, Eltron fall, merger off.

text.p: Shares of bar code technology companies Zebra Technologies Corp and Eltron International Inc fell Thursday after the two said they had terminated merger negotiations.
"For both companies, it means more competition," said Dick Davis of the equity research firm Richard Davis & Co.
Illinois-based Zebra and California-based Eltron last month signed a letter of intent to merge in a stock-swap, but they announced late Wednesday they had ended talks.
Eltron shares traded 5-1/4 lower at 33 and Zebra was off four at 26.
Earlier Thursday, Ed Kaplan, chairman and chief executive of Zebra, told analysts on a conference call that the merger fell through because of concerns over who would run the combined company.

Zebra said it is continuing to expand into the area of low-price bar code printers, an area in which analysts said Eltron is currently strong. Zebra said orders for its new printers are better than expected.
"I think the merger would have been for a plus for them (Zebra), but I think they can get to the same place on their own," said John Grangaard, an analyst for GS2 Securities.
"We're telling people to buy Zebra at these levels," Grangaard said, adding he has set a 12-month price target of $44 a share for Zebra.
Davis said Eltron is expected to continue its move into the mid-range price market as well.
"I think Eltron has some very interesting characteristics," Davis said, including quick time to market.
